title: Saul's Conversion, Paul in Damascus, Peter Heals Aeneas, Raises Dorcas

questions.question: Saul was still breathing threats and murder against the disciples. Where did he go to obtain letters to arrest followers of the Way?
options: To the high priest, requesting letters to the synagogues in Damascus
To Pilate, requesting a Roman warrant for their arrest
To Herod Agrippa, for authorization to pursue them to Antioch
To the Sanhedrin directly for orders to arrest all Christians
questions.correctAnswer: To the high priest, requesting letters to the synagogues in Damascus
questions.explanation: Acts 9:1-2 (ESV): "But Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest and asked him for letters to the synagogues at Damascus..."

questions.question: As Saul neared Damascus, a light from heaven flashed around him. What voice did he hear?
options: "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"
"Saul, Saul, why do you fight against God?"
"Saul, Saul, I have chosen you to serve me."
"Saul, your sins are forgiven, rise and serve."
questions.correctAnswer: "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"
questions.explanation: Acts 9:4 (ESV): "And falling to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?'"

questions.question: When Saul asked "Who are you, Lord?", the voice replied "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting." Then what instruction was he given?
options: "Rise and enter the city, and you will be told what you are to do."
"Go to the apostles in Jerusalem and confess your sins."
"Return to the high priest and renounce your mission."
"Fast in the wilderness for three days as preparation."
questions.correctAnswer: "Rise and enter the city, and you will be told what you are to do."
questions.explanation: Acts 9:6 (ESV): "But rise and enter the city, and you will be told what you are to do."

questions.question: What was the physical effect on Saul when he rose from the ground?
options: He could not see; he was blind and had to be led by hand into Damascus
He could not stand and had to be carried by his companions
He could not speak for three days and communicated by signs
His hands were paralyzed and he could not write for one week
questions.correctAnswer: He could not see; he was blind and had to be led by hand into Damascus
questions.explanation: Acts 9:8 (ESV): "Saul rose from the ground, and although his eyes were opened, he saw nothing. So they led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus."

questions.question: For how many days was Saul blind in Damascus without eating or drinking?
options: Three days
Seven days
One day
Forty days
questions.explanation: Acts 9:9 (ESV): "And for three days he was without sight, and neither ate nor drank."

questions.question: God sent a disciple named Ananias to Saul. In the vision God gave Ananias, what was Saul doing?
options: He was praying and had seen in a vision Ananias coming and laying hands on him to restore his sight
He was fasting and weeping over his past persecution
He was studying the Scriptures in the house of Judas
He was dictating a letter to send to the high priest
questions.correctAnswer: He was praying and had seen in a vision Ananias coming and laying hands on him to restore his sight
questions.explanation: Acts 9:11-12 (ESV): "...for behold, he is praying, and he has seen in a vision a man named Ananias come in and lay his hands on him so that he might regain his sight."

questions.question: Ananias was reluctant because of Saul's reputation. What did the Lord say Saul was destined to be?
options: A chosen instrument to carry God's name before the Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel
A great apostle to the twelve tribes of Israel and beyond
A high priest of the new covenant appointed by Christ himself
A prophet greater than Elijah who would prepare the final day
questions.correctAnswer: A chosen instrument to carry God's name before the Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Acts 9:15 (ESV): "But the Lord said to him, 'Go, for he is a chosen instrument of mine to carry my name before the Gentiles and kings and the children of Israel.'"

questions.question: After Ananias laid hands on him and Saul regained his sight, something fell from his eyes. What does Acts describe this as?
options: Something like scales
A white film
A grey veil
Thick darkness
questions.explanation: Acts 9:18 (ESV): "And immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he regained his sight."

questions.question: What did Saul immediately begin doing in the Damascus synagogues after his baptism?
options: Proclaiming Jesus saying "He is the Son of God"
Teaching about the kingdom of God generally
Apologizing for his past persecution of believers
Reading Moses and the prophets to show Jesus is Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: Proclaiming Jesus saying "He is the Son of God"
questions.explanation: Acts 9:20 (ESV): "And immediately he proclaimed Jesus in the synagogues, saying, 'He is the Son of God.'"

questions.question: When the Jews of Damascus plotted to kill Saul, how did the disciples help him escape?
options: They let him down through an opening in the wall, lowering him in a basket
They disguised him in Roman soldier's clothing
They arranged for a merchant caravan to smuggle him out
They created a distraction at the gate while Saul slipped out
questions.correctAnswer: They let him down through an opening in the wall, lowering him in a basket
questions.explanation: Acts 9:25 (ESV): "but his disciples took him by night and let him down through an opening in the wall, lowering him in a basket."

questions.question: In Jerusalem, the disciples were afraid of Saul. Who vouched for him to the apostles?
options: Barnabas
Ananias
Silas
John Mark
questions.explanation: Acts 9:27 (ESV): "But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles and declared to them how on the road he had seen the Lord, who spoke to him..."

questions.question: Peter visited the saints in Lydda and found a man named Aeneas who had been bedridden for eight years because he was paralyzed. What did Peter say to heal him?
options: "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you; rise and make your bed."
"In the name of Jesus of Nazareth, stand up and walk."
"Be healed by the power of the Holy Spirit; rise, Aeneas."
"The Lord Jesus commands you: take up your bed and walk."
questions.correctAnswer: "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you; rise and make your bed."
questions.explanation: Acts 9:34 (ESV): "And Peter said to him, 'Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you; rise and make your bed.' And immediately he rose."

questions.question: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (or Dorcas) who died. What was she known for?
options: She was full of good works and acts of charity, especially making clothes for widows
She had hosted the disciples in her home during persecutions
She was a prophetess who had foretold the spread of the gospel
She was the first woman to be baptized in Judea
questions.correctAnswer: She was full of good works and acts of charity, especially making clothes for widows
questions.explanation: Acts 9:36,39 (ESV): "She was full of good works and acts of charity... All the widows stood beside him weeping and showing tunics and other garments that Dorcas made..."

questions.question: Peter knelt and prayed beside Dorcas' body, then said what to raise her?
options: "Tabitha, arise."
"Rise in the name of Jesus."
"Dorcas, rise and live."
"Come back to us, sister."
questions.explanation: Acts 9:40 (ESV): "But Peter put them all outside, and knelt down and prayed; and turning to the body he said, 'Tabitha, arise.' And she opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter she sat up."

questions.question: After Saul's conversion, what was the state of the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria?
options: It had peace and was being built up, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit
It continued to face intense persecution but grew rapidly
It was divided over how to treat Saul, a former persecutor
It experienced a period of miraculous healings and deliverances
questions.correctAnswer: It had peace and was being built up, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Acts 9:31 (ESV): "So the church throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace and was being built up. And walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, it multiplied."

key_verse_text: "Go, for he is a chosen instrument of mine to carry my name before the Gentiles and kings and the children of Israel."
